title: Unified Inference: Q4 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary:

This document bundles the Q4 2026 product overview, high-level PRD and requirements, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging notes, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private). It is intended for product, engineering, GTM, and support teams preparing for H1 2027 customer engagements and commercial launches.

Overview:

- Product name: Unified Inference (UIF) 
- Scope: A single API and operational surface that provides predictable latency and cost controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Goal this quarter: Stabilize the v3 routing & fallback subsystem, deliver Redwood Optimize integration (v6) cost recommendations into Console, and launch the new tiered pricing & packaging model for Dedicated.

Core product positioning and target outcomes:

1) Developer-first, production-grade inference: consistent API, streaming, tool-calling, and structured output.
2) Cost-aware controls: automatic and manual batching, quantization profiles, caching, route-based cost policies.
3) Multi-environment parity: same developer experience for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Key metrics and targets (Q4 2026):

- Latency P95 (text-gen, hosted): <= 350ms at 1sps for sequence length 512
- Dedicated capacity utilization target: 70-85% average across reserved pools
- Cost reduction target (Redwood Optimize recommendations applied): 18-25% token cost reduction for qualifying workloads
- Adoption target: 15 enterprise Dedicated contracts including M+ customers by EOY

PRD: Requirements (high-level):

Objective: Deliver a cohesive product that reduces cost and increases reliability for customer inference workloads while keeping the API and SLAs familiar to existing Redwood customers.

Must-have requirements:

- API compatibility: New SDK and REST endpoints must be backward compatible with existing generation/chat/embeddings endpoints. Any breaking changes require clear migration guide.
- Routing and fallback: Implement policy-driven routing with first-class fallback to cheaper or regional model variants when SLOs at the requested model cannot be met. Policies must be configurable per-customer and per-route.
- Redwood Optimize integration: Expose actionable quantization and batching recommendations in Console with one-click apply for Dedicated and hosted preview.
- SLA and telemetry: Update SLOs, add token-level cost attribution in Console, and surface model rollback triggers based on quality regressions (via evals).
- Packaging: New tiered pricing for Dedicated (Standard / Performance / Enterprise) with clear commit sizes and burst allowances.

Nice-to-have requirements:

- Auto-gradation: graceful functionality degradation (compress responses, fall back to lower-accuracy variants) based on load.
- Trial mode for Dedicated: 14-day trial capacity for qualifying startups.

Design specifications (architecture and behaviour):

1) Routing & Fallback Subsystem

- Components: Policy store (per-customer), Router, Capacity-aware scheduler, Fallback selector, Telemetry exporter.
- Policy primitives: preferred_models (ordered), latency_slo_ms, cost_budget_per_1000_tokens_usd, region_preferences, enable_fallbacks (bool).
- Behaviour: Router evaluates policies at request arrival. If preferred model queueing time + estimated runtime > latency_slo, Router selects next compatible variant that meets policy constraints. Fallbacks must preserve tokenization/response formatting (transform layers if necessary).

2) Redwood Optimize Console Integration

- UI surfaces: workload profile page, recommendation panel, forecasted cost delta, estimated quality delta, apply-button with preview.
- Backend: Batch-analysis job (daily) that consumes route-level traces and metric histograms, outputs candidate quantization profile and batching config.

3) API and SDK changes

- New per-request fields: routing_policy_id (string), cost_limit_usd (float, optional), prefer_low_cost (enum: none|balanced|aggressive). All SDKs to default to previous behavior.

4) Observability and Rollback

- Metrics to add: model_variant_switch_rate, fallback_rate, estimated_cost_per_request_usd, per-route_quality_score (derived via evals).
- Alerts: fallback_rate > 5% for > 15m triggers paging to SRE. per-route_quality_score drop > 3 points triggers product review.

Roadmap and themes (Q4 2026 - Q2 2027):

Themes by quarter:

- Q4 2026 - Stabilize routing & optimize fallbacks; Redwood Optimize UI integration (v6); Dedicated pricing & packaging launch.
- Q1 2027 - Private deployment parity for routing features; autoscaling policy templates; rollout of trial Dedicated program.
- Q2 2027 - Advanced cost controls (dynamic quantization switching), per-customer model catalogs, and improved RL-based scheduling for latency-sensitive workloads.

Milestones & dates:

1) 2026-11-30: Routing v3 alpha deployed to staging + e2e tests
2) 2026-12-15: Redwood Optimize integration behind feature flag in Console; docs published
3) 2026-12-20: Pricing & packaging public announcement draft (internal review)
4) 2027-01-15: Dedicated tiered pricing go/no-go decision
5) 2027-02-28: Private parity release v1 (routing & fallback)

Pricing & packaging notes (summary):

Objective: Align pricing with customer value (latency & predictability) while simplifying buying motions for Dedicated.

Hosted (existing):

- No change to per-token base rates for on-demand. Add priced Redwood Optimize recommendations as an optional add-on ($0.005 per analyzed request) - pilot only.

Dedicated (new tiered model):

- Standard: committed capacity (vCPU/GPU pool) with 30% discount vs on-demand, basic SLAs (99.5% uptime), burst: 10%
- Performance: higher commit, 50% discount, SLO 99.8%, burst: 25%
- Enterprise: custom pricing, dedicated account support, optional on-prem connector and extended retention.

Packaging constraints and terms:

- Commit lengths: 6 / 12 / 24 months with increasing discounts; early termination fees apply.
- Burst allowance: percentage of committed throughput allowed for free bursts per month; additional usage billed at an elevated overage rate.

Commercial playbook (short):

1) Small customers: encourage on-demand + Optimize add-on trial.
2) Mid-market: recommend Standard Dedicated with 6-12 month commit; offer onboarding credits.
3) Enterprise: Performance or Enterprise tier with tailored SLA and onboarding program.

Release notes (v2026.12.20):

This release is a documentation-centric release that coincides with a public pricing announcement and a staged rollout of feature-flagged capabilities in Console and the Router. No breaking API changes are included in this release.

Highlights:

- Public docs: New Console UX for Redwood Optimize recommendations (feature-flagged).
- Router: v3 routing & fallback in staging. Production rollout scheduled after canary.
- Pricing: Drafts for tiered Dedicated pricing available to sales & finance.
- Telemetry: New metrics instrumented (fallback_rate, model_variant_switch_rate, estimated_cost_per_request_usd).

Known limitations and follow-ups:

- Auto-gradation prototype not included in this release - planned Q1 2027.
- Quantization recommendation accuracy will be improved in Q1 2027 after additional workload sampling.
- Console one-click apply is feature-flagged and limited to a pilot group; broad enablement after user feedback.

Rollout and canary plan:

1) Internal dogfood (internal services + Redwood apps) - 2 weeks
2) Canary customers (3 customers across different workload profiles) - 4 weeks
3) Gradual ramp to 25% of hosted traffic - monitor fallback_rate and latency P95
4) Full rollout pending go/no-go based on metrics and customer feedback

Appendix: Example configuration tables

1) Routing policy example (table):

Field | Type | Example | Notes
------|------|---------|------
policy_id | string | policy-prod-lowlatency | immutable id
preferred_models | list[string] | ["redwood-13b-v2","redwood-8b-q4"] | ordered preference
latency_slo_ms | int | 350 | P95 desired
cost_budget_per_1000_tokens_usd | float | 0.21 | approximate
enable_fallbacks | bool | true | allow fallback variants

2) Quantization profile (table):

profile_id | shrink | quant_bits | estimated_cost_delta
-----------|--------|------------|--------------------
q-default-8bit | 0.95 | 8 | -22%
q-safe-6bit | 0.9 | 6 | -34%
